  Scenario: AC9 A fact with a personal-data field outside the schema is refused and its value is never logged (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a fact of the run carrying a field outside the schema that holds a personal-data value
    When it is consumed
    Then the append is refused with MSG-P7-009 naming the offending field, and no entry, no chain_seq and no inbox row is written
    Then the fact is dead-lettered with an alert, the field is named in the incident and no personal-data value is copied into a log line

  Scenario: AC10 A correction is appended and the entry it corrects stays unchanged (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the entry of the key "CASE_EVENT:EV-CASE-0777-01" exists for case "RW-2026-000777"
    When a correction of that entry is consumed with corrects_entry_id naming the corrected entry
    Then a new entry is appended with the next chain_seq and corrects_entry_id naming the corrected entry
    Then the corrected entry is unchanged and both entries stay in the chain

  Scenario: AC11 Two consumers of one partition take the chain head in turn (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given two consumers of the same partition of rwb.decision-record.v1 attempt the chain head of case "RW-2026-000777" at the same time
    When both appends are taken
    Then the ledger serialises the head and one entry takes the next chain_seq
    Then the other consumer retries and appends after it, and no two entries share a chain_seq

  Scenario: AC12 An amend or delete through the service login or the schema owner role is refused and audited (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given an entry of case "RW-2026-000777" exists
    When an UPDATE or a DELETE of that entry is attempted through the rwb-decision login or through the schema owner role
    Then every statement is refused by the missing grant or by the append-only rule of the table
    Then each refused attempt is written to the ACE audit log and the entry is unchanged
